messages:
anya (Eng-Platform): Heads-up — we're aligning on new per-model/route SLO dashboards for latency/throughput. Need input from runtime/console/infra on metric names, tags, and sampling to avoid cardinality explosion.
marc (Eng-Runtime): +1. Current thought: emit base metrics at request level and roll up in ingest. Proposed names: `redwood.request.latency_ms`, `redwood.request.ttft_ms`, `redwood.request.tokens_generated`, `redwood.request.generation_seconds`, `redwood.request.batch_size`, `redwood.request.kvcache_hit` (0/1).
jess (Eng-ML): For quality regression linking we also want `model_version` and `quantization` labels. but those increase cardinality — can we tag coarse quantization buckets like `q4/q8/fp16`?
marc (Eng-Runtime): yes, use `model_version` only for sampled traces; add `model_variant` as low-cardinality (e.g. `base/quantized/fallback`). `quantization` as `q8/q4/fp16` is fine.
leo (Eng-Infra): Where are these metrics landing? prometheus or clickhouse? prometheus histograms don't like extremely high cardinality.
anya (Eng-Platform): Proposal: realtime panels (1m/5m) served from Prometheus for p50/p95/p99 and TTFT; long-term rollups (1h/24h) into ClickHouse for historical heatmaps and retention.
nina (SRE): Agree. Suggest we keep Prom labels limited to `model_name`, `route`, `region`, `deployment_tier` (hosted/dedicated/private), `fallback` (true/false). No `instance_id`.
samir (Eng-Console): For console UX we need per-route dropdowns and allow scoping by model_name + route + region. Also want tokens/sec heatmap by model across regions. How do we compute tokens/sec?
jess (Eng-ML): tokens/sec = tokens_generated / max(generation_seconds, 0.001). Emit both fields and compute in query: `tokens_per_sec = sum(tokens_generated)/sum(generation_seconds)` over the window.
rachel (Product): For SLOs, we plan to show p50/p95/p99 for latency and TTFT, plus tokens/sec and tokens/sec/cost. Default SLO thresholds: latency p95 < 500ms for small routes, p95 < 1s for large gen routes; p99 alerts at 2s. TTFT thresholds TBD per route.
marc (Eng-Runtime): Implementation note: runtime will emit latency as a histogram (buckets) and a separate summary for exact percentiles if we want. Prometheus histograms let us compute p50/p95/p99 with `histogram_quantile`. We'll emit `redwood_request_latency_bucket{le=...,model_name="...",route="..."}`.
leo (Eng-Infra): Important: limit bucket cardinality by using the same buckets across services and avoid per-model custom buckets. Also keep max bucket count small.
anya (Eng-Platform): Another cardinality control: sample 1% of low-traffic routes with full label set (model_version+request_id) and roll up the rest to aggregated model_name only. We can surface a sampling badge in the console.
samir (Eng-Console): UX request: for routes with sampling enabled show a toggle "Show sampled traces" and indicate estimated error due to sampling. Also allow switching windows (5m/1h/24h).
nina (SRE): Alerts: create composite alerts — p99 sustained over 5m for a route with traffic > X tokens/sec. Avoid noisy alerts on small routes. We need a cardinality-limited alerting key (route+model_name+region).
jess (Eng-ML): Also emit `fallback_count` metric when a request falls back to a lower-tier model. We want panels showing fallback rate by route and by model_variant.
marc (Eng-Runtime): We'll add `fallback` label and `redwood_request_fallback_total` counter. Also emit `inflight_requests` gauge and `request_queue_time_ms` to distinguish scheduling delays vs compute latency.
leo (Eng-Infra): Storage plan: Prometheus (short-term, 30d) with 15s scrape, use remote_write to ClickHouse for aggregated aggregates with 1m resolution and a daily rollup job. ClickHouse will store tokens/sec heatmaps and retention for 365d.
anya (Eng-Platform): Dashboard panels checklist: 1) p50/p95/p99 latency (line) per model/route, 2) TTFT p50/p95/p99, 3) tokens/sec (heatmap) by model, 4) tokens-per-cost (tokens / $) estimate, 5) fallback rate, 6) queue time vs compute time stacked.
rachel (Product): We also need an "SLO health" single-number card per route (green/yellow/red) and an ability to annotate rollouts/canary windows.
samir (Eng-Console): UX: add a "Compare model variants" mode to overlay p95 lines for base vs quantized vs fallback.
nina (SRE): On traces: add exemplars to histograms linking to tracing URL (request_id) for slow p99 samples.
marc (Eng-Runtime): Will add exemplars for latency buckets and include `trace_id` as exemplar label. Need to ensure sampling rate of exemplars is configurable.
anya (Eng-Platform): Small open questions: - exact Prom metric names (histogram vs summary) - sampling percentage defaults - per-team alert thresholds - charting rollup windows. Can teams comment?
jess (Eng-ML): prefer histograms + exemplars. sampling: default 0.1% traces, 5% for high-traffic routes.
leo (Eng-Infra): default sampling ok. I'll draft ingestion limits and cardinality budget per route.
rachel (Product): I'll produce a default SLO matrix mapping route categories to p50/p95/p99/TTFT thresholds by EOW.
anya (Eng-Platform): Action items: @marc add metric names + example prometheus queries, @leo draft cardinality budget and ingestion plan, @samir wire mockups for compare/annotation UI, @nina propose alert rules. Ping me when PRs are up. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline started for `metrics/ingest` -> staging at commit 9f3b7d2
marc (Eng-Runtime): Will push a PR with metric naming and example `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_name, route, region))` in the next 24h.
anya (Eng-Platform): Thanks everyone — we'll sync again after the PRs land.
